stops.name: Rephidim, Jethro's counsel; the seventy judges
stops.campa: Jethro the priest of Midian comes to Moses in the wilderness, bringing Zipporah and her two sons whom Moses had sent back. Moses tells him all the LORD has done to Pharaoh, and Jethro rejoices and blesses the LORD. He sees Moses judging the people alone from morning to evening and warns him he will surely wear away: "The thing that thou doest is not good." He counsels rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens, to bear the small matters, that Moses bear only the great. Moses hearkens; the burden is shared. Then Jethro departs into his own land.
stops.quote: The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee.

stops.name: Sinai, the theophany; the thunder and the trumpet
stops.campa: In the third month they come to the wilderness of Sinai and camp before the mount. God calls Moses up and offers the covenant: if Israel obey, they shall be a peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests, an holy nation. The people are sanctified two days, their garments washed, bounds set about the mount. On the third morning there are thunders and lightnings, a thick cloud, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud, so all the people tremble. Mount Sinai is altogether on smoke, for the LORD descends in fire; the whole mount quakes greatly, and the trumpet sounds long and louder. Moses speaks, and God answers by a voice.
stops.quote: And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire.

stops.name: Sinai, the Ten Words spoken
stops.campa: Out of the fire and cloud God speaks all these words, the Ten, in the hearing of all the people: I am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me. No graven image; the Name not in vain; the sabbath kept holy; father and mother honoured; not to kill, nor commit adultery, nor steal, nor bear false witness, nor covet. The people see the thunderings and remove and stand afar off, and say to Moses, "Speak thou with us; but let not God speak with us, lest we die."
stops.quote: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

stops.name: Sinai, forty days in the cloud; the pattern of the Tabernacle
stops.campa: Moses draws near to the thick darkness where God is, and the elders behold the God of Israel, under His feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone. Moses goes up into the mount, and a cloud covers it; the glory of the LORD abides upon Sinai, and to Israel below the appearance is like devouring fire on the top of the mount. Moses enters the cloud and is in the mount forty days and forty nights, while God shows him the pattern of the Tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the lampstand, and gives him the two tables of testimony, written with the finger of God.
stops.quote: And Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights.

stops.name: Sinai, the golden calf; the tablets shattered
stops.campa: Below, the people gather to Aaron: "Make us gods, which shall go before us; for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him." He takes their golden earrings, fashions a molten calf, and they say, "These be thy gods, O Israel," and rise up to play. On the mount God tells Moses to go down, for the people have corrupted themselves. Moses descends with the two tables; he sees the calf and the dancing, and his anger waxes hot, and he casts the tables from his hands and breaks them beneath the mount. He burns the calf, grinds it to powder, strews it on the water, and makes them drink.
stops.quote: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.

stops.name: Sinai, the plague of the calf; the sons of Levi
stops.campa: Moses stands in the gate of the camp: "Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me." All the sons of Levi gather to him, and at his word go through the camp, and there fall about three thousand men. The LORD plagues the people for the calf. Moses goes up again and pleads: "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written." He asks to see God's glory, and is hidden in a cleft of the rock while the glory passes, beholding the back parts, for no man sees God's face and lives.
stops.quote: Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.

stops.name: Sinai, the second tables; the shining face
stops.campa: Moses hews two tables of stone like the first and goes up again forty days and forty nights, eating no bread, drinking no water. The LORD passes before him and proclaims His name: merciful and gracious, longsuffering, forgiving iniquity, and He writes again the words of the covenant, the ten commandments. Moses comes down from the mount with the two tables, and knows not that the skin of his face shines from talking with God. Aaron and the people are afraid to come nigh him; so he puts a veil upon his face, and takes it off when he goes in to speak with the LORD.
stops.quote: The skin of his face shone while he talked with him.

stops.name: Sinai: the Tabernacle raised; the glory fills it
stops.campa: The willing-hearted bring their offerings, and Bezaleel and Aholiab, filled with the spirit of God in wisdom, make all the work: the boards of shittim wood, the curtains of blue and purple and scarlet, the ark, the table, the golden candlestick, the altars, the laver, the priestly garments and the breastplate of twelve stones. On the first day of the first month of the second year, Moses rears up the Tabernacle. Then a cloud covers the tent, and the glory of the LORD fills it, so that Moses cannot enter. By day the cloud is on the tent, by night fire, in the sight of all Israel throughout their journeys.
stops.quote: Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

stops.name: Taberah and Kibroth-hattaavah, the fire and the graves of lust
stops.campa: The people complain, and the fire of the LORD burns among them and consumes the uttermost parts of the camp; Moses prays, and the fire sinks. They call the place Taberah, burning. Then the mixed multitude lusts for flesh and weeps for the fish and cucumbers of Egypt, loathing the manna. The LORD takes of the spirit on Moses and puts it on seventy elders, who prophesy; Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp. A wind brings quails from the sea, but while the flesh is yet between their teeth a plague smites the greedy, and they bury them at Kibroth-hattaavah, the graves of lust.
stops.quote: Would God that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!

stops.name: Hazeroth, Miriam's leprosy and Moses' meekness
stops.campa: At Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married, saying, "Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?" And the LORD hears. Now the man Moses is very meek, above all the men upon the earth. The LORD calls the three out, comes down in the pillar of cloud, and declares that with Moses He speaks mouth to mouth, not in dark speeches. His anger kindles; Miriam becomes leprous, white as snow. Moses cries, "Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee," and after seven days shut out, she is received again.
stops.quote: With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold.

stops.name: Kadesh-barnea, the twelve spies and the fainthearted report
stops.campa: From Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran Moses sends twelve men, a prince of every tribe, to spy out Canaan. Forty days they search it, and return bearing a cluster of grapes on a staff between two, and pomegranates and figs. It flows with milk and honey, they say, but the people are strong, the cities walled, and there are giants, the sons of Anak; "we were in our own sight as grasshoppers." The congregation weeps all night and murmurs to return to Egypt. Only Caleb and Joshua rend their clothes and say the land is good and the LORD is with them. The people would stone them.
stops.quote: And there we saw the giants... and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.

stops.name: Kadesh, the sentence of forty years
stops.campa: The glory of the LORD appears in the tent; He would smite the people with pestilence, but Moses pleads His name and mercy among the nations, and God pardons yet decrees the sentence: none of the men who saw His glory and His miracles in Egypt and tempted Him these ten times shall see the land; their carcases shall fall in the wilderness. Forty years, a year for each day the spies searched the land, until all that generation die, save Caleb and Joshua. The ten evil spies die of the plague. Presuming to go up in the morning, the people are smitten by the Amalekites and Canaanites down to Hormah.
stops.quote: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.
